doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: You cannot go back: the reunion and nostalgia
summary: The 30-years-later reunion tour wasn't the same; he looks forward.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So anyway, but I really feel that, sincerely, that we just happened to be the right guys at the right place. Same thing I feel about Miles and his groups. Or any group that is put together and the sound is there and the feeling is there, they’re the right people for the right — you know. And that’s why you ask me about that reunion CD. You can’t go back man. That’s 30 years. And we went on tour, right? And it wasn’t the same. All us guys 30 years older, and it just — the moments weren’t there. You can’t go back, that’s what I feel anyway. Nostalgia is fantastic, but in your emotions, that’s all we’ve got is memories, you know, from one moment to the next. And you try to make as many pleasant moments as you possibly can have, because hey when you look back that’s what
you want to look at. But you can’t capture feelings. It’s over. So you’ve got to look forward. Hey turn the corner, turn the page.
It’s almost like to recreate what that was you would have had to set aside all your experiences from then on to try to get back to that.
